records.declaration: #define AUDIT_ALWAYS   2	/* Generate audit record if rule matches */
#define AUDIT_FILTER_EXIT	0x04	/* Apply rule at syscall exit */
#define AUDIT_SOCKADDR		1306	/* sockaddr copied as syscall arg */
#define IN_DONT_FOLLOW		0x02000000	/* don't follow a sym link */
#define IN_MOVED_FROM		0x00000040	/* File was moved from X */
#define IN_MOVED_TO		0x00000080	/* File was moved to Y */
#define IN_ONLYDIR		0x01000000	/* only watch the path if it is a directory */
#define NLM_F_ACK		0x04	/* Reply with ack, with zero or error code */
#define NLM_F_DUMP_INTR		0x10	/* Dump was inconsistent due to sequence change */
#define NLM_F_MULTI		0x02	/* Multipart message, terminated by NLMSG_DONE */

semantics.claim: AUDIT_GET.backlog counts audit_queue only. kauditd separately services audit_hold_queue, audit_retry_queue and the main queue; a record can already be dequeued into an in-flight unicast or waiting in retry/hold while main backlog is zero. EAGAIN can move records to retry. Overflow increments audit loss. The timestamp/serial identifies related audit pieces; serial is an atomic unsigned counter, not a contiguous delivery certificate. auditsc emits EOE after an event's records, but EOE closes only that group and establishes no ordering against other producers or reply threads. Consumer limits are 64 incomplete groups, 1000ms per group, 256 queued events and 1048576 bytes; malformed, unknown, unattributable, missing-end, loss or capacity failures are terminal. No selected interface fences all producer, main, hold, retry and socket delivery queues. Empty backlog, EAGAIN, healthy status and a complete local group cannot establish a native barrier.
limits: No all-producer audit drain or ordering fence is supported by these finite sources.
Audit serial wrap/reset or incomplete/unknown groups fail; no universal gap-free serial predicate.
Group/queue/time ceilings are fail-closed bootstrap policy, not kernel delivery promises.

semantics.claim: AUDIT_GET returns audit_status health, not rules: receiver pid, enabled, failure, rate_limit, backlog_limit, lost, main backlog, feature bitmap and wait fields. Consumer policy requires the original exclusive receiver, enabled=1, failure=0 (AUDIT_FAIL_SILENT), rate_limit=0, backlog_limit=256 and unchanged lost at most every 100ms. AUDIT_SET receiver registration checks the caller's own TGID and rejects replacing a healthy receiver. Initial PID namespace and CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL are required for status/control/list requests. CONFIG_AUDIT depends on NET; CONFIG_AUDITSYSCALL depends on AUDIT and HAVE_ARCH_AUDITSYSCALL; audit=1 selects boot-time audit enablement. These are source prerequisites, not proof of the installed configuration or privilege isolation. failure=0 suppresses audit_panic diagnostics only: kauditd_printk_skb independently prints raw non-EOE records on hold/retry failure paths, so silent status does not prove absence of raw kernel diagnostics.
limits: Healthy AUDIT_GET cannot establish unchanged rules, delivery completion or compiled kernel/config provenance.
Lost-counter increments are terminal; failure=0 never authorizes ignoring loss.
Raw kernel diagnostic suppression is unproved; no raw console or audit-log export is authorized.
All four roles retain zero initial-namespace capabilities and unchanged inherited FDs/syscall policy.

semantics.claim: AUDIT_LIST_RULES is separate from AUDIT_GET. audit_list_rules_send snapshots lists under audit_filter_mutex and asynchronously unicasts AUDIT_LIST_RULES records with NLM_F_MULTI, the request sequence and kernel nlmsg_pid=0, ending in NLMSG_DONE. audit_krule_to_data zeroes the fixed structure, exports flags/action/field_count, fields/values/fieldflags and the whole 64-word mask. The bootstrap protocol must bound kernel-sender, matching-sequence enumeration to 16 rule records, 65536 total bytes and 100ms at installation, every barrier and each health check; demultiplex replies and events on the original stream without loss. Compare one AUDIT_FILTER_EXIT/AUDIT_ALWAYS rule, field_count=1, fields[0]=AUDIT_ARCH, fieldflags[0]=AUDIT_EQUAL, values[0]=AUDIT_ARCH_AARCH64, no key/string buffer, zero unused fields/values/fieldflags, and exactly the native bind/listen/clone/clone3/execve/execveat/ exit/exit_group/setns/unshare/mount/umount2/pivot_root/chroot/mknodat syscall mask. AUDIT_WORD(nr)=nr/32 and AUDIT_BIT(nr)=1U<<(nr%32); no fork/vfork entries exist in this native table. Reject extra/changed/duplicate/missing rules, wrong flags/operator, errors, truncation, foreign sender/sequence and missing DONE. These bounds are consumer policy, not kernel deadlines. Exhaustive installed-rule certification is UNAVAILABLE: allocation failure in audit_krule_to_data breaks a filter-list iteration, while audit_make_reply failure skips a record; a later allocation can still produce NLMSG_DONE. The list sender also does not propagate every netlink_unicast result. A complete-looking matching list cannot certify absence of an omitted extra rule. Native admission remains closed.
limits: SUPPORTED wire inspection is not exhaustive installed-rule certification under allocation failure.
NLMSG_DONE, ACK and locally requested mask bytes cannot upgrade this UNAVAILABLE result.
No reference-supported lossless event/reply demultiplexing or all-producer drain is established.
Any new syscall, field, mask, dependency or enumeration mechanism needs separate reference review.

semantics.claim: The finite source tuple is NETLINK_AUDIT unicast, NETLINK_ROUTE link/address/route multicast, NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT group 1 and one inotify instance. It requires exactly four bootstrap-only nonblocking CLOEXEC descriptors and one wakeup pipe pair, supervised by descriptor-free PollSelector while referring to original role pipes without donation. Linux AArch64 little-endian LP64 constants/layouts come from the cited UAPI, native syscall selection and retained AAPCS64 scalar/aggregate rules; anonymous union members overlap, and flexible-array tails add no fixed-size bytes. The old coverage supplies already accepted socket/errno/fcntl definitions, not new source semantics. No selected mechanism synchronizes audit production/hold/retry/list replies, route producers, suppressed/filtered uevents and inotify producers, or orders them with the worker's final launch effect. Even exhaustive audit rule certification is unavailable under allocation failure. Return NATIVE_EVENT_BARRIER_UNAVAILABLE and NATIVE_EFFECT_FENCE_UNAVAILABLE; no EventCheckpoint or native launch authority can be minted from EAGAIN, backlog=0, NLMSG_DONE, EOE, contiguous SEQNUM, snapshots or inert tests. Pinned guest Python PollSelector/socket/inotify wrapper behavior is unqualified.
limits: UNAVAILABLE is a reviewed source limitation, not a missing record, passing empty stream or operational approval.
The initial audit PID namespace, all role namespace visibility and exclusive receiver/rules remain required.
No new role privilege, protocol exception, FD donor, alternate telemetry, acquisition or persistent audit service is authorized.
Native population, kernel/config identity, Python wrappers, signing, worker payload, fixtures and real B1 qualification remain unperformed.
No receiver-empty observation orders all source producers against the separate worker final effect.

semantics.claim: The selected inotify instance watches /etc and /etc/resolv.conf by retained inode marks; directory notifications include relative child names. Watch creation resolves a pathname once; IN_DONT_FOLLOW controls final symlink following and IN_ONLYDIR requires a directory. IN_MASK_CREATE refuses an existing watch. Cyclic watch IDs identify marks, not path history. Atomic replacement can leave a file watch on the old inode; directory moves, creation/deletion and watch loss must fail, never transparently rearm. Consecutive queued events with equal mask, wd and name are coalesced; the comparison does not include the rename cookie, so cookie is not a unique event sequence. Queue overflow or allocation failure queues IN_Q_OVERFLOW (wd=-1); ignored watches emit IN_IGNORED then leave the ID map, and unmount/watch/source death is terminal. Names are padded to the fixed event size with NUL bytes; readers must bound len and the complete payload. EAGAIN describes the current local queue, not completion of all inode producers. Coalescing, asynchronous delivery and inode/path replacement preclude proving every intermediate write or a fence.
limits: Watch IDs/cookies cannot count every intermediate change or prove a filesystem-wide drain.
CONFIG_INOTIFY_USER=y and namespace/path/FD provenance are native prerequisites, not source-derived runtime facts.
Exact watched inode/path identity, watch disappearance, replacement and partial setup require original cleanup ownership.
Existing accepted O_CLOEXEC/O_NONBLOCK coverage supplies IN_CLOEXEC/IN_NONBLOCK aliases; role FD rules do not change.

semantics.claim: Rtnetlink multicast nlmsg_seq can be 0, or copied from a triggering request; it is not a global increasing event sequence. Link/address/route sources fill sequence independently. Netlink receiver congestion reports ENOBUFS and increments socket drops unless reporting is suppressed; receive buffers can produce MSG_TRUNC, and sockaddr_nl sender/group comes from kernel skb metadata. Check actual kernel sender and truncation, never trust only the message header. Bootstrap must not suppress ENOBUFS and must terminate on any truncation/loss/death. Notifications are asynchronously queued to sockets; EAGAIN or an empty receiver queue does not synchronize pending producers or other event sources. There is no supported route drain or combined ordering fence in these selected sources.
limits: nlmsg_seq=0 is valid notification data, not a sequence-gap detector or a heartbeat.
Kernel sender/header checks do not create a cross-source producer ordering guarantee.
Loss remains terminal; there is no retry-away-loss or polling fallback.

semantics.claim: The selected NETLINK_ROUTE groups are link, IPv4/IPv6 interface addresses and IPv4/IPv6 routes: sockaddr_nl masks 1|16|256|64|1024. RTM_NEWLINK and RTM_DELLINK are generated for registered device changes with registration-state checks. RTM_NEWADDR and RTM_DELADDR use per-network-namespace IPv4/IPv6 address notifications. RTM_NEWROUTE and RTM_DELROUTE use the namespace route multicast groups; IPv4 address-related route changes build fib_config for insertion/deletion. This supports observing the cited notification paths, not exhaustive NIC/device history, arbitrary namespaces or an atomic topology snapshot. Fixed rtmsg/ifinfomsg/ifaddrmsg headers and aligned rtattr payloads must be bounded; any unexpected accepted mutation latches failure even if a subsequent snapshot reverts it.
limits: Namespace visibility for all original roles must be independently established.
The selected producer paths do not prove every intermediate topology change is delivered.
No dump/resample or newly installed source renews event generation or admission.

semantics.claim: NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT sends action/devpath and NUL-separated environment records to group 1. uevent_suppress, the kset filter and missing subsystem can return before SEQNUM assignment. Under uevent_sock_mutex the u64 global counter is incremented before broadcast; tagged events select a network namespace, untagged broadcasts traverse eligible sockets. ENOBUFS/ESRCH are suppressed in the producer return, so receiver loss must still fail. Discontinuous, duplicate, malformed or reset SEQNUM is terminal, but contiguous received values cannot prove complete device coverage or absence of suppressed changes. CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the target network namespace also permits rebroadcast of userspace-origin data with kernel portid=0 and a new SEQNUM; trusted privilege isolation is required, and sender=0 alone cannot prove a physical kernel device transition. No device drain or effect fence is established by this notification mechanism.
limits: Suppression/filtering happens before numbering; contiguous SEQNUM is not complete coverage.
Global numbering and namespace selection can cause gaps unrelated to receiver overflow; still fail closed.
The u64 sequence must be bounded without float conversion; no native Python wrapper qualification is inferred.
SUPPORTED describes finite notification semantics only, not authenticity against privileged injectors or a fence.
